proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the absence of ontological orientation'?

entities.label: AbsenceOfOntologicalOrientation
entities.rationale: The phrase 'absence of ontological orientation' most naturally denotes a theoretical or conceptual content — a characterization of a system or agent as lacking directedness toward foundational ontological commitments. As a propositional or theoretical content that can be instantiated and copied across contexts, it fits BFO_0000031 (Generically dependent continuant). It is not a quality (BFO_0000019) because it is not a determinate measurable property inhering in a single bearer; it is not a disposition (BFO_0000016) because absence of a disposition is not itself a disposition in BFO; and it is not a process (BFO_0000015). The best defensible placement is as a GDC representing a theoretical characterization or descriptive content. However, this placement is uncertain and listed in open_questions.

open_questions: Is 'absence of ontological orientation' intended as: (a) a theoretical/philosophical claim or description (suggesting BFO_0000031, GDC), (b) a quality of a system or agent — i.e., the measurable lack of a certain directedness (suggesting BFO_0000019, Quality), (c) a privation or negative disposition — i.e., the absence of a disposition toward ontological grounding (which BFO does not natively support as a positive entity; absences are not modeled as positive BFO entities), or (d) a process or state of affairs in which an agent or system operates without ontological orientation (suggesting BFO_0000015)?

BFO 2020 does not natively support 'absences' as positive ontological entities. Should this be modeled instead as the negation of an existing class (e.g., the complement of some OntologicalPrimacyClaim or NormOntologicalCondition), or as a quality of deficiency inhering in a LegalInstitution or LegalWorld individual?
Is this intended to describe a property of a specific individual (e.g., a particular legal system lacking grounding), or a general class of situations/contents?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asks for BFO classification of 'the absence of ontological orientation,' which is philosophically challenging because BFO 2020 models positive entities and does not have a native category for absences or privations. The most defensible classification, treating it as a propositional or theoretical content characterizing systems lacking ontological directedness, is as a Generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031) — a kind of theoretical description or characterization that can be instantiated across different contexts and bearers. An alternative is Quality (BFO_0000019) if understood as a measurable deficiency property inhering in a specific bearer such as a LegalInstitution. A third option is that this should not be minted as a positive entity at all, but rather expressed through negation or complement axioms in OWL. No relations are proposed until the user clarifies intended use and scope.
